info.title: Roma API
info.description:
The user's own Roma workspace: tasks, notes, projects, typed lists (collections) and automations. A place an AI chat can store work, pick it up again and keep knowledge between conversations.

Every call acts as the signed-in person, on their own workspace. Authenticate with a Roma API key (Settings → Connections) or an OAuth access token as a bearer. The same operations are available over the Model Context Protocol at /mcp; this REST surface exists for tools that speak HTTP rather than MCP (Zapier, Make, n8n, a script).

get.description: Use this at the start of a conversation that involves the user's Roma workspace, or when you need an overview of it. Returns, in one call: how Roma works; the user (name, timezone, today's date and local time); what they asked the AI to remember about them; their projects; overdue, due-today, in-progress and upcoming tasks; unsorted tasks; recently touched notes; their collections with columns; their automations with the last run; and the last few days of activity. Everything comes with ids for follow-up calls. It is an overview, not the full data: use search, list_tasks, get_note or get_collection_items for depth. Pass focusProjectId to scope the task sections to one project.

parameters.description: Optional project UUID. Scopes the task sections to that project; the rest stays workspace-wide.

post.summary: Create many tasks in one call
post.description: Create many tasks in one call, the way to hand Roma a list of outstanding work (a list the user dictates, an import, the work another agent hands over). Each row takes the same fields as create_task; a call-level projectId files every row that names none. The tasks are stored as written and indexed for search; no AI pass runs unless `enrich` is true, which then behaves like create_task. A row's `externalId` (the caller's own id for it) makes re-sending safe: the same externalId returns the task already made, reported under `existing`, instead of a duplicate. One bad row never fails the batch; it is reported under `failed` with its reason.

The body merge mode controls how `description` combines with the existing body — adding text appends/prepends; it never replaces unless you explicitly ask it to.

description.description: Body text to merge in per `mode`. Omit to leave the body unchanged; null to clear it.

mode.description: How `description` merges: 'append' (default, at the bottom), 'prepend' (at the top), 'insertAfter' (right after the line named in `anchor`), or 'replace' (swap the whole body — only when the user explicitly asked to rewrite it; never to add content; requires confirmReplace: true).

confirmReplace.description: Required (true) for mode 'replace': confirms the user explicitly asked to swap the WHOLE body, deleting everything in it. Never pass it on the user's behalf without that explicit ask.

anchor.description: For mode 'insertAfter' only: a verbatim snippet of the existing line to insert after. Errors if not found.

get.summary: Search notes, tasks and list rows
get.description: Search the user's Roma workspace — their notes, tasks, typed lists and the rows inside them — by meaning or keyword (hybrid semantic + keyword retrieval). Use this when the user asks about their own information, plans or anything they may have saved, and before adding something that may already exist. Their wording often won't match their notes' wording; the semantic arm bridges that gap (and across languages). Returns the best-matching passage per item; get_note returns a note's full text. An empty result means nothing relevant is saved. Not for general web knowledge.

post.description: Add rows to a collection, many in one call (the import path). Values are keyed by column id or name; a select value may be its label or option id, a multiSelect value is an ARRAY of them, and unknown labels become new options.
